newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Sep 6 - The seasonel upturn in palm production is finally underway after two months of stagnation in June-July. Partial data available indicate CPO production in August rose 11 percent or 80,000 tonnes to an estimated 801,000 tonnes. This exceeds our pevious estimate of a seven percent rise. Production was still flat in first-half August but picked up strongly in the second half. This was most evident in the South (Johore), the east coast region and East Malaysia which collectively accounted for 71 percent of production in the country in January-July.

Field reports and our recent bunch count surveys indicate the likelihood of continuing good harvests in these leading producing areas in September/October. Weather conditions remained favourable with frequent widespread showers and occasional thunderstorms. In line with the improved supply situation, offtake of CPO is estimated to have increased some 15,000 tonnes to 770,000 tonnes. There are indications most, if not all, refineries were operating at or near full capacity and enjoying good margins.

With production exceeding offtake, CPO stocks at end August are estimated to have risen to 435,000 tonnes from 401,600 tonnes month earlier. In contrast, PPO stocks are estimated to have dropped slightly to 345,000 tonnes. Total palm oil stocks thus amounted to an estimated 785,000 tonnes or some 30,000 tonnes more than month earlier. Compared to August last year, palm oil stocks were substantially higher by 210,000 tonnes. Concomittant with the better than expected production, palm oil exports in August also remained robust surging to an all time high of an estimated 675,000 tonnes.

This is 30,000 tonnes more than July and also comfortably surpassed the previous all-time record exports of 658,200 tonnes posted in January '94. Buoyed by robust export performance in August, CPO futures surged as much as 68 ringgit in just two days with November posting an intraday high of 1,266 ringgit on Monday September 2 before settling at 1,249 ringgit. Over the last three days the market attempted to consolidate with November flucting between 1,256 and 1,225 ringgit and settling at 1,243 ringgit yesterday.

A slowdown in the pace of new export sales in recent days coupled with lack of leads in other world vegoil markets had a restraining impact on the upward momentum of palm oil price. Some major importers like India and Pakistan also found prevailing palm oil price too high relative to their domestic market price. November/January RBD Olein was quoted at $562.50 yesterday. Latest conflict between Iraq, U.S. had resulted in continuing suspension of Iraqi crude oil exports. Earlier Iraqi oil exports were expected to resume mid-September.
The latest development would hurt further Iraq's financial capacity to pay for imports of palm oil and other food and medicine.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
